title: Using Emoji Captions? Keep the Spoken Words Readable
description: Add emoji captions without losing spoken words. Review meaning, readability and the saved video when styling captions on an iPhone.
direct: Keep the complete spoken words in your captions. Add an emoji when it supports the meaning and does not slow down reading.
figureAlt: A complete sentence about tea remains readable beside a supporting tea emoji.

cards.decision.heading: Start with the decision
cards.decision.body: Creative captions can be useful and enjoyable, yet decoration competes with reading. Caption-user research on TikTok identifies both expressive value and problems with non-verbatim substitutions. Preview your own video without sound before deciding how much styling it needs.
sections.detail-0.heading: Words carry the message
sections.detail-0.body: A tea icon can reinforce a sentence about tea. Replacing a key verb or name with a symbol asks viewers to interpret a new message. Likewise, an amused icon can suggest a tone that the speaker did not intend. Section 508 guidance emphasizes accurate captions and meaningful audio information; a decorative style alone does not establish accessible delivery.
sections.detail-1.heading: Know the styling options
sections.detail-1.body: The current release includes editable transcripts, emoji styles, word highlights and clean subtitles. One single-video Emoji export can be tried free; further Emoji exports require Pro. Optional AI emoji matching sends caption text online only after consent and has an on-device fallback. Always review the result; automatic matching is not proof that every emoji fits.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: What if an emoji suggests the wrong tone?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: Remove the effect or choose a clean caption style. Keep the speaker’s wording and check how the line reads with audio muted.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: Should I replace a repeated word with an emoji to save space?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: Keep the spoken word if it carries meaning. Try a simpler style or review the line in context before removing words.

steps.step-1.text: Generate captions in Subtitle Maker: Just Captions and correct the transcript first. Preserve the actual spoken wording before choosing an Emoji or word-highlight style.
steps.step-2.text: Watch a short passage at ordinary phone size with audio muted. Check that each word remains easy to follow and that the emoji matches the context rather than changing the meaning.
steps.step-3.text: If the effect competes with a name, instruction or serious statement, try a clean style. Export the captioned video and check the saved file again, including fast speech and scene cuts.
